items.title: Jack Kelly Interview, 1963-11-17
items.q: The interviewee narrates a childhood story involving 'Chris' and 'his dad' and 'my uncle'. The interviewer clarifies that 'Chris' was called 'Bud'. The interviewee does not claim a personal relationship with Bud, only narrating an event where he was a participant/observer.

ctx.x: The fellow got the piece of railroad out and he put it, he said, pick it up. So he picked it up. When I get it, he swam it like around and around like this, you know. He put it down. So his dad was busy, so he had a little wagon and he just run, you know, little cut, you know, with the line, with the line, running up. So he told my uncle, he said, call Chris back there.
So he called him Bud, my uncle called him Bud, you see. He said, Bud, he said, he wants you up in the front. I said, all right. He called me over there. He said, come here.

He said, Chris, I got a bet on you. He said, if you win, I'm going to give you a hundred feet. I'm going to give you a hundred feet. He said, yeah, look what you got. He said, this boy will pick up this railroad. He said, you know, I'm going to have a point of his knees. I said, okay. The old man picked it up, he come all the way up, straight up. Take it like that, from the back there. He said, boy, you got yourself a little bit. That's about it, I'm giving you an idea, I pop for you and the rest. Yeah, you do,…
